notes:
Quick CRM summary / fragments from calls:
- Prospect: Sunward Vault AI — underwriting platform for commercial insurance. Heavy PII, retention rules, strict data residency for EU and UK customers.
- Primary ask: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed networking) w/ KMS integration (HSM-backed CMK), CloudTrail/CloudWatch export to customer's logging account, and per-request audit logs.
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 120ms for short-chat flows (context ~512 tokens). Throughput: peak 400 concurrent chat sessions, burst to 1200 for renewals season.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high — will trade some latency for cost; interested in Optimize recommendations (quantization, batching).
- Model preferences: want Redwood-curated open models first; will validate against fine-tuned BERT/encoder-decoder models for reranking/embeddings. Needs deterministic routing + fallback to smaller quantized models during low capacity.
- Networking: prefer no inbound internet access to inference nodes. Suggested design: Private subnets per AZ, private endpoint (interface ENI) for control plane connectivity, NAT gateway in a dedicated subnet for outbound update checks (restricted egress), optional managed bastion for debugging. Customer asked about possible PrivateLink endpoint instead of NAT for tighter outbound control.
- KMS: require customer-managed keys in AWS KMS with HSM (multi-region key replication not allowed by legal). Must ensure key policies support Redwood service principal and customer admin.
- Audit logging: must forward all inference audit events (prompt hashes, request metadata, model version) to customer's CloudWatch Logs / S3 with 3650d retention; also require immutable audit exports in case of incident.
- Data residency: for EU customers, inference logs and request payloads must remain in eu-west-1; need confirmation that Redwood Private control plane can be deployed inside customer's VPC or via private control plane with VPC peering.
- Compliance: provided SOC2 report and ISO docs; legal opened VRQ (SEC-1298).
- Quote from SecOps: "We cannot allow any managed keys outside our account; HSM-backed CMK and clear audit path are non-negotiable."
- Internal notes: strong enterprise opportunity — procurement flagged for May decision. Need architecture diagram + explicit KMS key policy example + networking checklist to move to demo.
architecture_fit_summary:
High level fit assessment (flat text):
- Fit: Good. Sunward's constraints align with Redwood Private (VPC) offering: private subnets, customer KMS, audit exports.
- Recommended topology: 3 AZ private subnets for inference pods, separate subnet for control-plane proxy (interface endpoint), NAT gateway(s) or egress via VPC endpoint/service-to-service PrivateLink. Use security groups to restrict inbound to the control-plane ENI only.
- Inbound/Outbound: No public inbound to inference nodes. Control plane to nodes via private endpoint over customer-managed VPC peering/Transit Gateway. Outbound updates restricted to allowlist of Redwood IPs or use customer proxy.
- Regions: Primary deploy: us-east-1; supplemental for EU customers: eu-west-1. Customer requires deployment templates for both regions and documentation on data partitioning.
- KMS integration: Customer-managed CMK in their AWS account; provide key policy template that grants Redwood role:EnableEncryptDecrypt, and supports CloudTrail key usage logs. If customer insists on HSM-only usage, confirm Redwood can accept key operations via AWS KMS (no key material transfer).
- Audit logging: ship model inference audit events to customer-owned CloudWatch/S3 via cross-account role. Provide option for realtime streaming to customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via Kinesis/Firehose.
- Gaps: need legal sign-off on key policy and support for PrivateLink instead of NAT. Also confirm support for air-gapped on-prem variant if procurement requests.
